chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The closest state of the servant to disbelief is that a man establishes brotherhood with another man upon the religion, so he counts his slips against him in order to rebuke him with them one day.
ai.seo_question: What is the closest state to disbelief in social relationships according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi is often cited to illustrate how superficial religious camaraderie can mask deep-seated arrogance and the desire for dominance, turning brotherhood into a tool for surveillance rather than mutual spiritual growth. It emphasizes that the intent behind social bonds is critical; when one records 'slips' (zallat) specifically to humiliate the other later, it reflects a lack of sincere love for Allah and His Prophet, which is a key indicator of impending kufr (disbelief). This concept is frequently linked to the practice of 'ghibah' (backbiting) and 'tadhallul' (seeking to lower the status of others) within the community of believers.
